info.title: Bitbybit CAD Cloud API
info.description: High-performance parametric CAD model generation API. Supports multi-format output (STEP, GLTF, decomposed mesh), pipeline execution, file-based conversion, and async job processing.

get.description: Returns the operational status of the Bitbybit CAD Cloud API, including service health and readiness. Requires no authentication, so it is suitable for uptime monitoring, load balancer probes and deployment smoke tests.

post.summary: CAD - execute a single operation
post.description: Runs a single CAD operation by its fully-qualified identifier.

post.summary: CAD - execute a chained pipeline
post.description: Runs multiple operations sequentially. Use '$ref:N' in params to reference step N's result.

post.summary: CAD - execute compound (parallel) operations
post.description: Runs several independent CAD operations in parallel as one compound task. Each sub-operation is executed on its own and produces its own downloadable result, so use this when the operations do not depend on each other - for a sequence where each step consumes the previous one's output, use the chained pipeline endpoint instead. Returns 202 with a compound task id; poll it and download the per-sub-task manifest when it completes.

get.description: Lists every parametric model available for generation, by name. Use the returned names with the definitions and generation endpoints to discover each model's parameter schema and defaults before submitting a job.

post.summary: Models - batch-fetch definitions
post.description: Returns parameter schemas and defaults for the requested model names.

post.summary: Models - execute a parametric model
post.description: Generic endpoint - works for any registered model. See model-specific endpoints for fully typed parameters. Always returns 202 with a task ID for polling.

post.summary: Models - generate a batch
post.description: Creates a compound task with one sub-task per item. Each item can have different parameters but shares the same output config.

get.description: Returns parameter schema, types, defaults, and limits for the specified model.

post.summary: Models - build a Dragon Cup
post.description: Parametric dragon-scale textured cup with twisted lofted body, voronoi-like skin cells, and configurable shell thickness. All parameters are optional - defaults produce a ready-to-print model.

post.summary: Models - build a Phone Nest
post.description: Parametric 3D-printable desktop phone holder/stand with a lofted cradle surface, optional ornamental perforations, and a phone mock-up shape. All parameters are optional - defaults produce a ready-to-print model.

post.summary: Convert - STEP to glTF (.glb)
post.description: Simple STEP → glTF conversion using a previously uploaded file. Requires the 'convert' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID.

post.summary: Convert - STEP to glTF (.glb), advanced options
post.description: Full-control STEP → glTF conversion with fine-grained mesh, export, and coordinate options. Requires the 'convert' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID.

post.summary: Convert - STEP to Draco-compressed glTF (.glb)
post.description: STEP → glTF conversion with Draco geometry compression using a previously uploaded file. Requires the 'convert' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID.

post.summary: Convert - STEP to Draco-compressed glTF (.glb), advanced options
post.description: Full-control STEP → glTF conversion with Draco geometry compression. Combines fine-grained mesh, export, and coordinate options with Draco quantization controls. Requires the 'convert' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold a face to flat geometry
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal unfold: flattens a single developable face (by index) of an uploaded STEP shape. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the flattened geometry is delivered as the task's output files.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold a face, metrics report
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal analysis: computes the unfold metrics report (developability, area, ...) for a single face of an uploaded STEP shape. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the JSON report is delivered in the task metadata.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold all solids to flat geometry
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal unfold: loads every solid in an uploaded STEP file and flattens each to a flat pattern. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; every flat is one part of a single output per format, named after its solid, so a nesting call reads one part per flat.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold all solids, metrics report
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal analysis: computes per-solid unfold metrics for every solid in an uploaded STEP file. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the JSON report array is delivered in the task metadata.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold all solids, geometry + report
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal unfold, full workflow: flattens every solid in an uploaded STEP file AND returns per-solid metrics in one call. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; every flat is one part of a single output per format, named after its solid, and the per-solid report array is delivered in the task metadata.

post.summary: Sheet metal - unfold all solids and nest the flats on sheets
post.description: Proprietary sheet-metal unfold and true-shape nesting in one call: flattens every solid in an uploaded STEP file and nests the flat patterns on sheets straight away, without writing them to a file and reading them back. Left out, the sheets are sized for the flats and the spacing and margin are scaled to them; 'fileUnit' reads a file whose header names the wrong unit. Every length is in millimetres. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the nested sheets come in the requested formats as on POST /api/v1/cad/pro/nesting/nest, 'flat-meshes' gives each solid's flat triangulated where it was unfolded, the NestingReport (each part naming its solid) is the metadata result, and the per-solid unfold report array is delivered in the task metadata.

post.summary: Nesting - place flat parts on sheets or a strip
post.description: Proprietary true-shape 2D nesting: places the flat parts of uploaded STEP files onto rectangular sheets or one strip, turning and flipping them as each part's options allow, with a spacing that holds on the true curved edges and parts placed inside other parts' holes. Every part a file places is a part, with each of its solids on its own, so an unfold's output gives one part per flat pattern; 'stepFileIds' gives the full rule. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; every used sheet is one compound of its placed parts, laid in a row on the XZ plane, combined into one output per format, and the NestingReport (placements with their transforms, each part as read, what was left and why, totals) is delivered as the metadata result.

post.summary: Nesting - read parts without nesting them
post.description: Reads the parts of uploaded STEP files as nesting would and reports each one's file, kind, outline size, area and cut length, or why it cannot be nested. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the NestingInspection is delivered as the metadata result.

post.summary: Drawing - draw a sheet or a set of sheets
post.description: Proprietary 2D drawing sheets from a 3D model: lays out views of the parts of an uploaded STEP file on a standard or custom sheet, lined up with a base view at a scale that fits, with hidden lines dashed, sections with their cuts hatched and a title block; when the plan asks, also dimensions, holes with a hole table, a parts list with balloons, the flat pattern of a sheet-metal part, the annotations the file stores (AP242) and a revision table. A plan is one sheet or a set: a list of sheets, or a rule that makes one from the file's product structure. Every setting has a default, so a body with only 'stepFileId' draws a default sheet; POST /api/v1/cad/pro/drawing/inspect returns the plan with every setting spelled out. A plan too large for the body is uploaded as a JSON file and named by 'planFileId'. The paper is measured in millimetres; the lengths a sheet prints are in its 'units', millimetres or decimal inches, the STEP file's own unit when the plan names none, and a set in inches is written as a DXF and an SVG in inches, while its PDF keeps the paper's millimetres. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the sheets come in the requested formats (PDF when left out, a page for each sheet; DXF and SVG with the sheets side by side), a format that cannot be written is left out and named in the task metadata's 'outputsLeftOut' with the reason, and the DrawingSetReport (the plan with every sheet written out, each sheet's place, report and, on a continuation sheet, its pagination, the warnings) is delivered as the metadata result. The task metadata also sums what the sheets report of how they read: 'floors' (the readability floors broken), 'continued' (the continuation sheets) and 'exactEstimate' (the seconds the exact method was predicted to take on CAD Cloud for the sheets drawn by sight), each only when reported.

post.summary: Drawing - read a model without drawing it
post.description: Reads the model of an uploaded STEP file as a drawing would, without drawing: how many parts it holds and its size, the first sheet's plan with every setting resolved, whether its views fit and the layout they take, the scale each standard sheet would allow, sections the model could be cut by, the views the file saved, every part with its name, and every sheet of the plan written out. The set's plan, edited or as it is, is ready to send to POST /api/v1/cad/pro/drawing/draw. Requires the 'cad' API key scope. Returns 202 with a task ID; the DrawingInspection is delivered as the metadata result.

post.summary: Files - request an upload URL
post.description: Returns a pre-signed URL for uploading a file via PUT.

200.description: The same bytes were uploaded and confirmed under this key before (matched by sha256): the existing confirmed file, ready to reference. No PUT is needed.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of the files uploaded under your API key, newest first, with each file's id, original name, size, upload status and expiry. Use it to find the file id to pass to a conversion endpoint, and to check that an upload through a pre-signed URL actually completed before you reference it.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number. Defaults to the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many files to return per page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only files in this upload state: pending (a pre-signed URL was issued but the upload has not been confirmed), confirmed (the blob is stored and usable), or expired.

get.description: Returns metadata and download URL for a single file.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an uploaded file and the stored blob behind it. This cannot be undone, and any task result that still points at the blob stops resolving. Files also expire on their own, so call this only when you need the storage released sooner than that.

post.summary: Files - confirm upload
post.description: Confirms that the file was successfully uploaded to the pre-signed URL.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of your tasks, newest first, each with its id, kind, status, creation time and result link when finished. Filter by status to poll only what is still running, or by kind to separate model generation, STEP conversion, pipelines and compound runs. This is the endpoint to build a job dashboard on rather than polling every task id individually.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number. Defaults to the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many tasks to return per page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only tasks in this state. waiting and queued are not started yet, processing is running, completed has a downloadable result, failed carries an error, cancelled was stopped by you, and expired means the result has been cleaned up.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Return only tasks of this kind: cad for a single operation, model for a registered parametric model, convert-simple and convert-advanced for STEP conversions, pipeline for a chained run, compound for a parallel run.

ExecuteBody.description: Execute a single Bitbybit CAD operation. The operation runs asynchronously and returns a task ID for polling.

steps.description: Ordered list of CAD operations executed sequentially. Later steps can reference earlier results using '$ref:N' syntax. Supports map and choice control-flow steps.

outputs.description: Output format options applied to the final pipeline result. Supports json, csv, stl, 3mf in addition to standard formats. If omitted, raw result data is stored.

PipelineBody.description: Execute a chain of Bitbybit CAD operations sequentially. Supports $ref:N step references, $file:N file inputs, map iteration, and choice conditionals.

PipelineAnyStep.description: A pipeline step - either a plain operation, a map (iteration), or a choice (conditional).

type.description: Declares this step as a map (iteration) step

items.description: Source array to iterate over. Typically a '$ref:N' reference to a previous step that produced an array.

steps.description: Sub-steps to execute for each item. Use '$item' for the current element, '$index' for the iteration number.

reduce.description: Optional sub-steps to combine map results. Use '$mapResult' to reference the collected array of iteration outputs.

MapStep.description: Iterate over an array, executing sub-steps for each element. Produces an array of results (or a reduced value).

operation.description: Fully-qualified CAD operation identifier (e.g. 'occt.shapes.solid.createSphere'). Supports OCCT, Manifold, JSCAD, and vector/math operations.

params.description: Operation parameters. Use '$ref:N' (e.g. '$ref:0') to reference the output of a previous step by its zero-based index. Use '$file:N[:<format>][:<codec>]' to reference an input file's contents - <format> is one of text|buffer|uint8|json|base64 (default text), and the optional <codec> is one of raw|gunzip|auto (default raw) to decompress the file first; 'auto' gunzips only when gzip magic bytes are present, so '$file:0:text:auto' reads both plain and gzip-compressed uploads (e.g. .step and .stpz).

output.description: When true, this step's result is included in a separate result.json output alongside any shape files.

PipelineStep.description: A single step in a sequential CAD pipeline. Steps can reference outputs of earlier steps via $ref or input files via $file.

type.description: Declares this step as a choice (conditional) step

value.description: Value to compare. Typically a '$ref:N' reference to a previous step result.

operator.description: Comparison operator to apply between value and compareTo

compareTo.description: Value to compare against. Not required for 'exists' operator.

then.description: Sub-steps to execute when condition is true

else.description: Sub-steps to execute when condition is false. If omitted, produces null.

ChoiceStep.description: Conditional execution - evaluate a condition and run the matching branch.

ComparisonOperator.description: Comparison operator: 'eq' (equal), 'neq' (not equal), 'gt' (greater than), 'gte' (greater or equal), 'lt' (less than), 'lte' (less or equal), 'exists' (value is not null/undefined).

fileId.description: ID of a previously uploaded file (from POST /files/upload)

InputFileItem.description: Reference to an uploaded file to be used as input

formats.description: Output formats to generate. Supports standard CAD formats (step, stpz, gltf, decomposed-mesh) plus pipeline-specific formats (json, csv, stl, 3mf, brep, brep-binary).

meshPrecision.description: Tessellation precision for mesh-based outputs (decomposed-mesh and gltf). Lower values produce denser meshes.

gltfMeshPrecision.description: Override tessellation precision specifically for glTF output. When set, takes precedence over meshPrecision for glTF only.

adjustYtoZ.description: Turns a decomposed-mesh output from Y-up, as the server models, to Z-up. It applies to decomposed-mesh only: a STEP output is always written Z-up, so a STEP sent in comes back as it went in, a glTF output is always Y-up, as glTF asks, and a BREP output keeps the frame the shapes were modelled in, as occt.io.loadBrep reads it back.

includePipelineInMetadata.description: Include the full pipeline definition in metadata.json. Defaults to true. Set to false to exclude it for smaller metadata.

unit.description: The unit the pipeline's shapes are modelled in. Given, a STEP output is written at its true size in millimetres, so CAD tools open the shapes at the right size, and a glTF output is written in metres, the unit glTF viewers assume. Left out, the numbers are written as they are: STEP takes them as millimetres and glTF holds them unscaled. The other formats carry no unit and always hold the numbers as they are. A design build's documents state their own unit, and a unit given here must be the same.

PipelineOutputOptions.description: Controls which output formats are generated for pipeline results. Supports additional formats (json, csv, stl, 3mf, brep, brep-binary) beyond standard model outputs.

PipelineOutputFormat.description: Pipeline output file format. Includes all standard formats plus: 'json' (JSON data), 'csv' (CSV text), 'stl' (binary STL mesh - Manifold/JSCAD only), '3mf' (3MF mesh package - Manifold/JSCAD only), 'brep' (OpenCascade BREP as text) and 'brep-binary' (OpenCascade binary BREP, the smallest and fastest exact form, which keeps the numbering of faces and edges) - both OCCT only, without triangulation, and both in the frame the pipeline modelled the shape in (Y up), so occt.io.loadBrep and occt.io.loadBrepBinary read them back exactly as they were; a Z-up tool such as FreeCAD shows them lying on their backs, where a 'step' output stands upright.

UnfoldAndNestBody.description: Flatten every constant-thickness sheet-metal solid in an uploaded STEP file and nest the flat patterns on sheets in the same call: the per-solid unfold report, the nesting report and the nested sheets, without writing the flats to a file and reading them back.

sheets.description: The stock to nest onto: kinds of rectangular sheets, or one strip. Left out, one kind of sheet is sized for the flat patterns: at least twice as long as it is wide, holding the largest flat with its margins, large enough that all the flats fill about half of it, its sides rounded up. When every flat fits on standard 3000 x 1500 stock and that sheet would be larger, the standard stock is used instead.

quantity.description: How many copies of every flat pattern to place: the number of models to make. Defaults to 1. All copies together, this number times the number of flat patterns, stay within 100000.

allowFlip.description: Whether every flat pattern may be turned over (a half turn about an axis in its plane, never a mirror). Defaults to false.

spacing.description: The least distance kept between any two flat patterns, in millimetres, measured on their true shapes. Defaults to a gap sized to the flats: a fiftieth of the square root of their area, rounded to 1, 2 or 5 of its decade.

margin.description: The band along each sheet's edges that no flat pattern enters, in millimetres. Defaults to the gap sized to the flats, the same one the spacing takes when it is left out; a spacing that is given does not change it.

timeBudgetSeconds.description: How long the nesting may search; the best layout found by then is returned. Defaults to 5 seconds, at most 120.

tolerance.description: How far the straight chords that stand in for curved edges may stray from them, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files); the spacing still holds on the true curves. Defaults to 0.1.

evaluationBudget.description: Stop after this many placements are tried, which makes a run repeatable for one seed; the time budget still applies. 0 means no limit.

seed.description: The seed of the search's random choices. Defaults to 1.

sheetGap.description: The gap between sheets as they are laid out in a row in the output, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files). Defaults to a tenth of the widest sheet.

UnfoldNestingOptions.description: How the flat patterns of an unfold are nested: the stock, the copies, how each flat may turn, and the search settings. Every length is in millimetres.

height.description: The strip's width across, along y, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files). Its length along x is open and is what the nesting makes as short as it can.

cost.description: What the strip costs: one amount, added to the totals' cost whatever length the nesting uses. Defaults to 1.

NestingStrip.description: One strip of open length; it stands alone, never beside other stock.

width.description: The sheet's side along x, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files).

height.description: The sheet's side along y, in the parts' units (millimetres for parts read from STEP files).

quantity.description: How many sheets of this stock there are. Without it, as many as needed.

cost.description: What one sheet of this stock costs. Without costs, the stock that wastes least is opened first (each sheet costs its area).

angles.description: The turns a part may take, in degrees, such as [0, 180] for a grain direction; at most 720.

step.description: Turn in steps of this many degrees; it must divide 360 evenly (90 gives 0, 90, 180 and 270).

NestingRotations.description: How a part may turn on the sheet: a fixed list of angles, steps that divide a full turn, or any angle. Without it a part turns in steps of 90 degrees.

formats.description: Output formats to generate; each gives a separate downloadable result. The nested sheets come in the formats of NestingOutputFormat, and 'flat-meshes' gives each solid's flat pattern triangulated where it was unfolded, tagged with its solidIndex, for showing beside the model; a flat that could not be meshed has no mesh there but is nested all the same, and its unfold report entry says why in 'meshError'. Give 'step' or 'stpz', not both.

meshPrecision.description: Tessellation precision for mesh-based outputs (decomposed-mesh and gltf). Lower values produce denser meshes. Only ignored when output is limited to step/stpz formats.

gltfMeshPrecision.description: Override tessellation precision specifically for glTF output. When set, takes precedence over meshPrecision for glTF only.

adjustYtoZ.description: Turns the decomposed-mesh and flat-meshes outputs from Y-up, as the server models, to Z-up. It applies to those two only: a STEP output is always written Z-up, and a glTF output is always Y-up, as glTF asks.

unit.description: The unit the 'dxf' and 'svg' cut files are written in: 'mm' (millimetres, the default), 'cm' (centimetres), 'm' (metres) or 'in' (inches). The drawing is scaled into it and each file states it, a DXF in its header ($INSUNITS) and an SVG in its width and height, so CAD and cutting software open it at its true size. It changes those two files only. A 'step' or 'stpz' file stays in millimetres, because a STEP file states its unit in its header and CAD programs convert it on import. 'gltf', 'decomposed-mesh' and 'flat-meshes' are written as they would be without it, holding the millimetre numbers unscaled. The 'outlines' JSON, the nesting report, the unfold report and every length of the request stay in millimetres.

UnfoldAndNestOutputOptions.description: Which formats the nested sheets and the flat patterns are written in, their mesh quality, and the unit of the DXF and SVG cut files.

stepFileIds.description: IDs of previously uploaded STEP files (.step, .stp or gzip-compressed .stpz), at most 50 and 200 MB together. priority.description: Parts of higher priority are placed first, so they are the last to be left off when stock runs out. Defaults to 0.

plan.description: What to draw. The default sheet when left out. Not given with 'planFileId'.

planFileId.description: ID of a previously uploaded JSON file holding the plan (named .json or of type application/json), at most 32 MB, in place of 'plan': for a set written out past the 128 KB a request body takes. It is held to the same rules as 'plan', and a refusal names the field inside the file. Not given with 'plan'.

outputs.description: Output formats. Left out, the sheet is written as PDF.

modelFromTask.description: The id of an earlier draw or inspection of this same uploaded file, read in the same 'fileUnit', whose model to take: the parts are taken from the model that task kept instead of being read from the file again, which on a large file is most of what an inspection or a sheet takes, and the sheets are the same, byte for byte. The task must be this account's, completed and not expired, started with an API key of the same storage as this request's, and have kept its model, which its report says under run.model.kept; a task that does not qualify refuses the request before it is queued, saying why, with the error's details naming the field 'modelFromTask'. Should the kept model turn out unusable once the task runs, the file is read instead and run.model.notReused says why.

DrawingDrawBody.description: Draw a sheet, or a set of sheets, of the model in an uploaded STEP file: views laid out and aligned, hidden lines, sections with hatches, dimensions, holes, parts lists with balloons, flat patterns, the file's own annotations and a title block. A set is one PDF with a page for each sheet and one DXF and one SVG with the sheets side by side.

units.description: The unit every length the sheet prints is written in: 'mm', millimetres, or 'in', decimal inches. It covers the overall sizes, ordinates, diameters, radius callouts, the hole table, the bend table's radius, the flat pattern's sizes and a custom sheet's size in the title block, whose UNITS cell says MM or IN; angles stay in degrees. In inches an automatic scale comes from the inch series (1:2, 1:4, 1:8, 1:10, 1:20 and so on), and the DXF and SVG are written in inches; the PDF keeps the paper's millimetres, and the geometry, the plan's lengths and every number of the report stay in millimetres. Left out, the STEP file's own unit decides: a file in inches, by its header or by 'fileUnit', is drawn in inches, any other in millimetres.

decimals.description: The places a printed length is written to: in millimetres at most that many, 0 to 4, idle zeros and the point dropped (12.5, 12); in inches exactly that many, 1 to 4, with no zero before the point (.250, 1.500). 2 in millimetres and 3 in inches when left out. A plan that names no units and 0 places is refused when the file proves to be in inches.

front.description: What the view names mean: 'front' looks along this frame and the other names turn with it. Left out, a sheet is drawn from its part's own front, square to the part's own faces (its plain faces and the axes of its round ones, the space's axes when the part is square to them), looking along the axis it shows most of with its long side across: a plate looks along its thickness and a turned part across its axis. The resolved plan writes that front into the sheet. A sheet of a list keeps the plan's front, or the space's axes, unless it says turned. 'annotations' asks for the front most of the sheet's drawn annotations read upright from, when it draws them; annotations never choose or tilt a front otherwise.

parts.description: The parts to draw by number, each once, or 'all'. Left out or 'all', every part that holds a face when any part does: loose curves beside solids, such as the curves an AP203 file draws its notes with, are left out and counted in the report's model.faceless.

views.description: The views, the first being the base the others line up with; views a plan states are kept as stated. Left out, a sheet the plan or a rule makes gets the views that describe its part: a plate its front and one edge view, a turned part its side and its end, any other part front, top and right, each with the isometric, which may take a smaller scale of its own. A view that does not fit beside them at their scale goes to a continuation sheet, and when the principal views' annotation letters would be under 2.5 mm together, each principal view whose letters would read on a sheet of its own gets one (the front stays); each continuation sheet says why in its pagination. A sheet of a list that states no views gets front, top, right and isometric. Empty only beside a flat pattern, for a sheet of the flat pattern alone, or beside shared notes, for a sheet of the general notes alone.

lines.description: How hidden lines are found. 'auto', the default, keeps the exact method to a budget: it draws the sheet exactly when the exact method is predicted to take 10 s or less for all its views together on a native build of the kernel (about 12 s on CAD Cloud, whose kernel takes 1.2 times as long), and by sight otherwise. The prediction weighs the faces by what they cost the exact method: a freeform face (a B-spline or Bezier surface, an offset of one, or a surface turned from a B-spline or Bezier curve) weighs as 160 plain faces, more when its normals turn round more than once, as on a coil spring, and a torus up to as much as a freeform face. The report's run.chosenBy says 'budget' or 'within', and run.exactEstimate gives the predicted seconds on CAD Cloud, about, whenever a view was drawn by sight. On a sheet over the budget a view is drawn by sight even when a few faces cannot be meshed; they hide nothing, and a warning says so. 'exact' works from the geometry alone; 'sight' draws the model's own edges and decides what is hidden from a picture of its mesh, seconds where 'exact' takes minutes on a large assembly; 'mesh' draws the edges of a tessellation.

titleBlock.description: False for a sheet without a title block; true, or left out, for one with empty fields.

dimensions.description: 'auto' sizes the first view's width and height and the one size each top, bottom, left or right view of it adds; on a sheet of one part it also sizes every distinct outside diameter once, in the first view that sees it from the side, and calls out every distinct radius of a round once, in the first view that sees it end-on. 'ordinate' gives the same, except that the first view is measured by ordinates from the lower left corner of the part's box, the corner the hole table measures from, to each hole centre it sees end-on and to the far sides. Left out, a plan without 'sheets', like a sheet a rule makes, gets 'auto', and a sheet given in a 'sheets' list draws none unless it or the plan asks for them. False draws none.

holes.description: 'auto' recognises the holes (through, blind, counterbored, countersunk), draws their centre marks and lines, tags those the first view sees end-on and lists them in a hole table. Left out, a plan without 'sheets', like a sheet a rule makes, gets 'auto' on a sheet of one part, and a sheet given in a 'sheets' list draws none unless it or the plan asks for them. False draws none.

holeTable.description: True, the default, lists the holes 'auto' tags in a hole table; a table too long for its sheet is left out with a warning, and a set continues it on sheets of its own instead. False leaves the table out and keeps the tags and centre marks. Given as rows, the sheet is a hole table alone and takes no views, sections, dimensions, holes, flat pattern, balloons, annotations or parts list.

flat.description: True adds a sheet-metal part's flat pattern as a view, with its bend lines and a bend table; 'auto' does so only when the part unfolds cleanly with a bend that folds: a part whose unfold is not clean, such as a casting, gets none, and a warning says why. Only a sheet of one part has one. With a flat pattern, views may be empty: the sheet is the flat pattern alone. Left out, a plan without 'sheets', like a sheet a rule makes, gets 'auto' on a sheet of one part, and a sheet given in a 'sheets' list has none unless it or the plan asks for one. False leaves it out.

annotations.description: True draws the dimensions, tolerances, datums and notes the STEP file stores (AP242), each on a view that faces the plane it was made in, adding views for planes none of the plan's views faces, and turns a line of letters that would read from the top or the left to read from the bottom or the right. Only a sheet of every part draws them: the model's own where they stand and each product's once, at its first instance. Given as an object, 'product' and 'instance' name one product's annotations, drawn where that instance stands whatever parts the sheet shows (a set made by a rule names them so on the sheet of each product that has annotations), and 'addViews' and 'notes' false leave the annotations no view faces and the general notes to another sheet of the set. Annotations never turn the front unless 'front' is 'annotations'. False when left out.

shared.description: What the sheet shares with the other sheets of its part. A resolved set writes it; a plan seldom needs to: send it back as the set gives it.

partsList.description: True gives every assembly's sheet a list of what goes directly into it (item, name, quantity, the sheet it is drawn on) and, when the list has at most 40 rows, balloons pointing at them; a list too long for the sheet takes sheets of its own after it. Not true with a hole table alone. A list given as rows is drawn on every sheet. False, the default, draws none.

balloons.description: With a parts list of true, false leaves its balloons out. Given as items, balloons around one view of every sheet, or around one section when the plan has no rule.

sheets.description: Several sheets: a list, each sheet stating what it changes of the plan (a sheet stating only parts is drawn with everything else as the plan says), or a rule that makes the list from the model's structure. One sheet of the plan when left out. The settings at the top of the plan are laid under every sheet.

DrawingPlan.description: What to draw: one sheet, or a set of sheets. Every setting has a default, so an empty plan draws a default sheet; the inspect route returns the plan with every setting spelled out and every sheet of a set written out, ready to edit and send to the draw route. A request body takes at most 128 KB, so a set written out past that, of a model with hundreds of sheets or thousands of parts beneath every level, is uploaded as a JSON file and named in 'planFileId', or sent as its rule.

size.description: A standard sheet by name, or a custom one by its width and height in millimetres. A3 when left out.

orientation.description: Landscape when left out. Not given with a custom size, which is drawn as its width and height say.

projection.description: First-angle on ISO and custom sheets, third-angle on ANSI sheets, unless given.

scale.description: The sheet's scale. 'fill', the default, takes the largest scale at which every view fits from the scales ISO 5455 recommends and those GOST 2.302 adds (1:2.5, 1:4, 1:15, 1:25, 1:40, 1:75 and the like); 'auto' keeps to the preferred 1, 2 and 5 steps. A fixed scale that does not fit is refused with the scale and the sheet that would.

DrawingSheet.description: The sheet a drawing is laid out on.

DrawingScale.description: A drawing scale, numerator to denominator: 1 to 50 is { numerator: 1, denominator: 50 }. Between 1:1000 and 100:1.

origin.description: A point of the view's plane; the origin of the model's space when left out.

normal.description: The side the eye is on: the view looks back along it. For a section it is the side that is cut away.

direction.description: What runs to the right in the view. It need not be of unit length nor exactly square to the normal, but it may not be parallel to it.

DrawingFrame.description: A view frame in the model's space, which is Y-up as a STEP file is read: millimetres, an origin, a normal and a direction.

name.description: A named view of the front frame. Give one of name, frame and saved.

frame.description: A view by its own frame. Give one of name, frame and saved.

saved.description: A view the STEP file saved (an AP242 model view), by its name: the sheet looks along it with its up upward, captioned with its name and without hidden lines unless told otherwise. A name the file does not hold refuses the sheet. Give one of name, frame and saved.

hiddenLines.description: Whether hidden edges are drawn, dashed. True unless the view is the isometric one.

smoothEdges.description: Whether edges where faces meet without a crease, such as the ends of a fillet, are drawn as thin lines. True when left out; seams of round faces are never drawn.

scale.description: The view's own scale. A view with its own scale is placed freely instead of in line with the others.

DrawingView.description: One view of the model on the sheet.

label.description: The section's letter, as in SECTION A-A. No two sections share one.

frame.description: The cutting plane is the frame's plane. What lies on the normal's side is cut away and the rest is seen from there.

shownOn.description: The index of the view that carries the cutting-plane line. 0 when left out.

hatch.description: False for no hatch, true or left out for the default one.

spacing.description: Millimetres on paper between the hatch lines.

DrawingHatch.description: The hatch on what a section's plane cuts: ansi31 at 45 degrees, 3 mm apart, when left out.

date.description: A text like any other: nothing defaults to today, so the same plan draws the same sheet on any day.

approvedBy.description: Who approved the drawing, one of the fields ISO 7200 makes mandatory: shown as APPROVED BY in a row of its own when given.

documentType.description: What kind of document the sheet is, such as Assembly drawing or Detail drawing, one of the fields ISO 7200 makes mandatory: shown as DOCUMENT TYPE in a row of its own when given.

sheet.description: The sheet's number in a set, such as 2 / 7: shown as SHEET when given. A set of several sheets writes it into every title block.

quantity.description: How many of the part are made: shown as QTY when given. A set writes the model's count of the product a sheet shows.

DrawingTitleBlock.description: The fields of the title block. Every field is empty unless given.

DrawingRevision.description: One row of the revision table.

DrawingHoleTable.description: A hole table alone: the sheet is these rows and nothing else, in columns as a parts list alone stands. A set writes such sheets after a part's sheet whose hole table runs over it.

DrawingHoleTableRow.description: One row of a hole table, as texts: the hole's tag, its X and Y from the lower left corner of the part's box in the first view, its size and its depth. A text left out is empty.

kFactor.description: Where the neutral fibre lies in the thickness, 0 to 1. 0.5 when left out, as the unfold route takes it.

thickness.description: The sheet's thickness in millimetres; 0, the default, finds it.

auto.description: True draws the flat pattern only when the part unfolds with at least one bend, and says nothing otherwise.

DrawingFlat.description: How a sheet-metal part is unfolded for its flat pattern.

product.description: The product whose annotations alone are drawn, by the number the inspection's set gives it, whatever parts the sheet shows. Left out, the whole model's annotations, as true draws them on a sheet of every part.

instance.description: Which of the product's instances they are placed at, counted from 0 in the order of the model's structure, depth first. 0 when left out; given only with a product.

addViews.description: False adds no view for annotations that none of the plan's views faces: another sheet of the set draws them, and the report counts them in annotations.elsewhere instead of warning. True when left out.

notes.description: False leaves the general notes, those that belong to no shape, to another sheet of the set, counted in annotations.elsewhere the same way. True when left out.

DrawingAnnotatedProduct.description: Which of the annotations the STEP file stores a sheet draws, and where: one product's, moved to where one of its instances stands, or the whole model's; and whether views are added for them and the general notes drawn, or both left to another sheet of the set.

views.description: The views the pages of one sheet share, in their order: the automatic sizes, diameters and radius callouts of dimensions are decided over all of them, as one sheet of every view would give them, and each page draws those that fall on its own views (matched by frame), so no size is given on two pages.

notes.description: True makes the sheet the general notes alone, laid over its whole frame, for notes the first sheet had no room for; its views are then an empty list. False when left out.

DrawingShared.description: What a sheet shares with the other sheets of its part. A resolved set writes it into the pages of a sheet it paginated, a continuation sheet for each view that did not fit or would not read beside the others, for the callouts and balloons the first sheet had no room for, and for general notes, so the set, sent back, draws the same sheets. Not given on a parts list or a hole table alone.

view.description: The index of the sheet's view it stands around.

callout.description: A radius callout's text, such as 4X R10, or the X0 Y0 of a hole table's origin. Give a callout or a balloon.

balloon.description: A balloon's text, a hole tag such as A12 included. Give a callout or a balloon.

at.description: The point the leader points at, in the model's space.

centre.description: A radius callout's arc centre in the model's space, which leads it along the arc's radius as on its first sheet.

DrawingSharedMark.description: A radius callout or a balloon another sheet had no room for, drawn on this sheet with a leader to the point it marks.

view.description: The index of the sheet's view it stands around.

callout.description: A radius callout's text. Give a callout or a balloon.

balloon.description: A balloon's text, a hole tag included. Give a callout or a balloon.

DrawingLeftMark.description: A radius callout or a balloon of this sheet's view that another sheet of the set carries: left out here without a warning.

alone.description: True makes the sheet the list and nothing else: it shows no part and takes no views, sections, dimensions, holes, flat pattern or balloons.

DrawingPartsList.description: A parts list drawn above the title block.

product.description: The product the row lists, by the number the inspection gives it. A set keeps the row's sheet true by it: resolved, the row's sheet is where that product's first sheet stands in the set, or empty when no sheet shows it, so a set whose sheets were moved or removed is put right by resolving it again. The rows a set writes name their product; a row without one is left as given.

DrawingPartsListRow.description: One row of a parts list: as texts, the item number, the name, the quantity and the sheet the part is drawn on, and the number of the product it lists.

view.description: The index of the view the balloons stand around, sections not counted. 0 when left out.

section.description: The label of a section of the plan: the balloons stand around that section instead of a view and point at what its cut keeps. Give a view or a section, not both.

items.description: Each balloon's text and the parts it may point at; it points at whichever of them shows. An item none of whose parts shows gets no balloon and a warning.

DrawingBalloons.description: Balloons around one view or one section, each with a leader to a part it names.

units.description: The unit every length the sheet prints is written in: 'mm', millimetres, or 'in', decimal inches. It covers the overall sizes, ordinates, diameters, radius callouts, the hole table, the bend table's radius, the flat pattern's sizes and a custom sheet's size in the title block, whose UNITS cell says MM or IN; angles stay in degrees. In inches an automatic scale comes from the inch series (1:2, 1:4, 1:8, 1:10, 1:20 and so on), and the DXF and SVG are written in inches; the PDF keeps the paper's millimetres, and the geometry, the plan's lengths and every number of the report stay in millimetres. Left out, the STEP file's own unit decides: a file in inches, by its header or by 'fileUnit', is drawn in inches, any other in millimetres.

decimals.description: The places a printed length is written to: in millimetres at most that many, 0 to 4, idle zeros and the point dropped (12.5, 12); in inches exactly that many, 1 to 4, with no zero before the point (.250, 1.500). 2 in millimetres and 3 in inches when left out. A plan that names no units and 0 places is refused when the file proves to be in inches.

front.description: What the view names mean: 'front' looks along this frame and the other names turn with it. Left out, a sheet is drawn from its part's own front, square to the part's own faces (its plain faces and the axes of its round ones, the space's axes when the part is square to them), looking along the axis it shows most of with its long side across: a plate looks along its thickness and a turned part across its axis. The resolved plan writes that front into the sheet. A sheet of a list keeps the plan's front, or the space's axes, unless it says turned. 'annotations' asks for the front most of the sheet's drawn annotations read upright from, when it draws them; annotations never choose or tilt a front otherwise.

parts.description: The parts to draw by number, each once, or 'all'. Left out or 'all', every part that holds a face when any part does: loose curves beside solids, such as the curves an AP203 file draws its notes with, are left out and counted in the report's model.faceless.

views.description: The views, the first being the base the others line up with; views a plan states are kept as stated. Left out, a sheet the plan or a rule makes gets the views that describe its part: a plate its front and one edge view, a turned part its side and its end, any other part front, top and right, each with the isometric, which may take a smaller scale of its own. A view that does not fit beside them at their scale goes to a continuation sheet, and when the principal views' annotation letters would be under 2.5 mm together, each principal view whose letters would read on a sheet of its own gets one (the front stays); each continuation sheet says why in its pagination. A sheet of a list that states no views gets front, top, right and isometric. Empty only beside a flat pattern, for a sheet of the flat pattern alone, or beside shared notes, for a sheet of the general notes alone.

lines.description: How hidden lines are found. 'auto', the default, keeps the exact method to a budget: it draws the sheet exactly when the exact method is predicted to take 10 s or less for all its views together on a native build of the kernel (about 12 s on CAD Cloud, whose kernel takes 1.2 times as long), and by sight otherwise. The prediction weighs the faces by what they cost the exact method: a freeform face (a B-spline or Bezier surface, an offset of one, or a surface turned from a B-spline or Bezier curve) weighs as 160 plain faces, more when its normals turn round more than once, as on a coil spring, and a torus up to as much as a freeform face. The report's run.chosenBy says 'budget' or 'within', and run.exactEstimate gives the predicted seconds on CAD Cloud, about, whenever a view was drawn by sight. On a sheet over the budget a view is drawn by sight even when a few faces cannot be meshed; they hide nothing, and a warning says so. 'exact' works from the geometry alone; 'sight' draws the model's own edges and decides what is hidden from a picture of its mesh, seconds where 'exact' takes minutes on a large assembly; 'mesh' draws the edges of a tessellation.

titleBlock.description: False for a sheet without a title block; true, or left out, for one with empty fields.

dimensions.description: 'auto' sizes the first view's width and height and the one size each top, bottom, left or right view of it adds; on a sheet of one part it also sizes every distinct outside diameter once, in the first view that sees it from the side, and calls out every distinct radius of a round once, in the first view that sees it end-on. 'ordinate' gives the same, except that the first view is measured by ordinates from the lower left corner of the part's box, the corner the hole table measures from, to each hole centre it sees end-on and to the far sides. Left out, a plan without 'sheets', like a sheet a rule makes, gets 'auto', and a sheet given in a 'sheets' list draws none unless it or the plan asks for them. False draws none.

holes.description: 'auto' recognises the holes (through, blind, counterbored, countersunk), draws their centre marks and lines, tags those the first view sees end-on and lists them in a hole table. Left out, a plan without 'sheets', like a sheet a rule makes, gets 'auto' on a sheet of one part, and a sheet given in a 'sheets' list draws none unless it or the plan asks for them. False draws none.

holeTable.description: True, the default, lists the holes 'auto' tags in a hole table; a table too long for its sheet is left out with a warning, and a set continues it on sheets of its own instead. False leaves the table out and keeps the tags and centre marks. Given as rows, the sheet is a hole table alone and takes no views, sections, dimensions, holes, flat pattern, balloons, annotations or parts list.

flat.description: True adds a sheet-metal part's flat pattern as a view, with its bend lines and a bend table; 'auto' does so only when the part unfolds cleanly with a bend that folds: a part whose unfold is not clean, such as a casting, gets none, and a warning says why. Only a sheet of one part has one. With a flat pattern, views may be empty: the sheet is the flat pattern alone. Left out, a plan without 'sheets', like a sheet a rule makes, gets 'auto' on a sheet of one part, and a sheet given in a 'sheets' list has none unless it or the plan asks for one. False leaves it out.

annotations.description: True draws the dimensions, tolerances, datums and notes the STEP file stores (AP242), each on a view that faces the plane it was made in, adding views for planes none of the plan's views faces, and turns a line of letters that would read from the top or the left to read from the bottom or the right. Only a sheet of every part draws them: the model's own where they stand and each product's once, at its first instance. Given as an object, 'product' and 'instance' name one product's annotations, drawn where that instance stands whatever parts the sheet shows (a set made by a rule names them so on the sheet of each product that has annotations), and 'addViews' and 'notes' false leave the annotations no view faces and the general notes to another sheet of the set. Annotations never turn the front unless 'front' is 'annotations'. False when left out.

shared.description: What the sheet shares with the other sheets of its part. A resolved set writes it; a plan seldom needs to: send it back as the set gives it.

name.description: The sheet's name in the report; a sheet made for a product is named after it.

product.description: The product of the model the sheet documents, by the number the inspection gives it: its parts list rows and its quantity come from it.

turned.description: True turns the sheet to its own part's front, square to the part's own faces, when the sheet states no front of its own: the plan's front frame is dropped for it, while a front of 'annotations' is kept.

pagination.description: Why the sheet continues the one before it, as a resolved set writes it on each continuation sheet: a view that did not fit beside the principal views, or principal views whose annotation letters were too small together. Sent back with the set, it marks the sheet as a continuation, so the set reads back to itself.

partsList.description: A parts list of this sheet's own, or false for none, whatever the plan says.

balloons.description: Balloons of this sheet's own, or false for none.

DrawingSetSheet.description: One sheet of a set: the settings it states replace the plan's, except sheet and titleBlock, whose fields are laid over the plan's one by one.

auto.description: 'structure': the whole model, then each assembly and part in the order of the model's structure, every assembly followed at once by what goes into it; 'parts': the whole model, then every distinct part; 'assemblies': the whole model and every assembly, no part.

overview.description: Whether the first sheet shows the whole model, with 'parts'. True when left out; 'structure' and 'assemblies' always start with it.

turned.description: Whether every sheet the rule makes, the overview included, is turned to its own part's front; every sheet but the overview drops the plan's front frame, and a front of 'annotations' is kept by all. True when left out; false keeps every sheet on the plan's front, or the space's axes.

most.description: The most sheets to make; a model that takes more is refused, saying how many it would take. 500 when left out.

depth.description: How many levels of assemblies are opened: an assembly below it is drawn as one part and gets no sheets of its own. 64 when left out, the deepest a model is read to.

DrawingSetRule.description: Sheets made from the model's product structure, each product once, its instances counted as its quantity. The plan's sections are drawn on the overview sheet alone and every sheet draws a product of the model, so a plan with a rule takes no balloons around a section and no parts list or hole table alone.

formats.description: The files to write the sheet as; each gives a separate downloadable result. Left out, the sheet is written as PDF.

DrawingOutputOptions.description: Which formats the drawing sheet is written in.

DrawingOnlySheets.description: The sheets of the set to draw, by their index in it counting from 0, as the inspection's 'set' and a drawn set's report list them; the others are not drawn. Each sheet is drawn and written as it is in the whole set, its title block numbering it among all of them (SHEET 2 / 5) and its DXF and SVG in the unit the whole set's are, that of its first sheet, and the files hold only the sheets named, in the set's order, laid out as a set of their own; each sheet of the report gives its 'index' and the report gives 'setSheets', how many the whole set has. An index past the set's last sheet fails the task. Left out, every sheet is drawn. With the 'fingerprint' every sheet of an inspection's set and of a drawing carries, an app that keeps the sheets it drew asks only for those whose fingerprint it does not hold.

stepFileId.description: ID of the previously uploaded STEP file (.step, .stp or gzip-compressed .stpz), at most 200 MB. Every placed part of the file is a part of the drawing, numbered from 0 in the order the file's structure gives them.

fileUnit.description: The unit a STEP file's numbers are really in, when its header states another unit or none: some exporters write a model drawn in metres under a millimetre header. Each file is scaled from it, so the model is read in millimetres, the unit every length of the request and its results is in. A header naming no unit counts as millimetres; a file whose header names a unit other than mm, cm, m or in, or several different ones, is refused, since its unit is converted already. Left out, each file's own unit is used.

plan.description: A plan to resolve. The default sheet when left out. Not given with 'planFileId'.

planFileId.description: ID of a previously uploaded JSON file holding the plan (named .json or of type application/json), at most 32 MB, in place of 'plan': for a set written out past the 128 KB a request body takes. It is held to the same rules as 'plan', and a refusal names the field inside the file. Not given with 'plan'.

modelFromTask.description: The id of an earlier draw or inspection of this same uploaded file, read in the same 'fileUnit', whose model to take: the parts are taken from the model that task kept instead of being read from the file again, which on a large file is most of what an inspection or a sheet takes, and the sheets are the same, byte for byte. The task must be this account's, completed and not expired, started with an API key of the same storage as this request's, and have kept its model, which its report says under run.model.kept; a task that does not qualify refuses the request before it is queued, saying why, with the error's details naming the field 'modelFromTask'. Should the kept model turn out unusable once the task runs, the file is read instead and run.model.notReused says why.

DrawingInspectBody.description: Read the model in an uploaded STEP file for a drawing without drawing it: its parts and size, the plan with every setting resolved, the layout that plan gives, the sections it could have, the views the file saved ('savedViews'), every part with the name of its product ('parts') and every sheet of the plan written out ('set').

filename.description: Original filename including extension (e.g. 'part.step', 'model.obj'). Used for display and format detection.

contentType.description: MIME type of the file (e.g. 'application/step', 'model/gltf-binary'). Must match the actual file content.

bytes.description: Exact file size in bytes. Must match the Content-Length of the subsequent PUT to the upload URL. Maximum: 1 GB.

sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the file content. When provided, enables server-side deduplication - if an identical file was previously uploaded under this API key, the existing file is reused and no upload is needed.

FileUploadBody.description: Request a pre-signed upload URL. After receiving the URL, PUT the raw file bytes to it within the expiration window.

UnfoldReportError.description: Returned when a shape/face cannot be processed by the unfold.

meshError.description: Why the flat pattern has no mesh in the decomposed-mesh or flat-meshes result, when it could not be meshed. The flat is still in every other output and, on unfold-and-nest, in the nest.

UnfoldSolidReportItem.description: Sheet-metal unfold metrics for ONE solid (bend table + face roles + original->flat map). On failure, the ok:false branch still carries the partial diagnostics gathered before the failure.

flatLineStart.description: Where the bend's centre line starts on the returned flat pattern, in the flat's own frame: the middle of the bend zone, as long as bendLineLength. A sharp fold's is the edge its flanges share. Absent for a bend the layout cut, and for a 0-degree join of two coplanar panels, which draws no bend line.

flatLineEnd.description: Where the bend's centre line ends on the returned flat pattern.

flatLineMid.description: The middle of the bend's centre line on the returned flat pattern, where a bend tag stands.

direction.description: 'up' when the flanges fold towards the side the returned flat faces (+Y of its frame), 'down' when they fold away from it. A 0-degree join, which does not fold, reads 'up'.

kind.description: 'cyl' and 'cone' fold through a bend face of that surface; 'sharp' folds along a shared edge with no bend face (faceIndex -1, inner radius 0), and a 0 degree 'sharp' fold joins two coplanar panels.

UnfoldBend.description: One bend: line, angle, radii (inner/outer/neutral and per-end for cones), and developed lengths.

tangentDot.description: Bend candidates (cylinder/cone) only: best |flange normal · cylinder radial| over the flanges. ~1 = tangent fold, ~0 = cutout/hole wall.

bendOutcome.description: How the fold filter classified a bend candidate: 'fold' (kept), 'cutout' (rejected - not tangent / <2 flanges), 'duplicate' (dropped - one fold per flat pair), or '' (a bend face not on the reference side, never evaluated by the filter).

UnfoldFaceEntry.description: A classified source face: stable key (index + BRepGraph uid), role, and label anchors.

UnfoldPlaced.description: A sub-shape laid into the flat compound, mapped back to its source face (compound order).

UnfoldSolidReportError.description: Returned when a solid cannot be fully unfolded; carries the partial diagnostics gathered before the failure (classified faces with roles, detected thickness, warnings) so the reason can be inspected.

stock.description: The index of the stock in the options' sheets.

width.description: The sheet's width; for a strip, the length it used.

origin.description: Where the sheet's corner lies in the working space, Y up, the sheet on the XZ plane facing +Y. A STEP output turns this space to Z up.

NestingSheetEntry.description: One used sheet: its stock, where it lies in the working space, and how much of it the parts fill.

box.description: The part's box on its sheet as [minX, minY, maxX, maxY].

anchor.description: A point inside the placed part's material, for a label, in the working space (Y up).

transform.description: The 4 x 4 matrix, column by column, that moves the input part to its place in the working space (Y up); a STEP output is that space turned to Z up.

NestingPlacement.description: Where one copy of a part was placed.

file.description: Which uploaded file the part came from, as an index into stepFileIds; present on the nesting routes, which read parts from files.

solid.description: Which solid of the model the flat pattern was unfolded from, as its solidIndex in the unfold report; present on the unfold-and-nest route.

problem.description: Why the part cannot be nested: nullShape, notPlanar, notClosed, notPlate, unsupportedShape or invalidGeometry.

kind.description: What the part was read as: face, faces, solid, wire or wires.

depth.description: A plate's thickness; 0 for a face or a drawing.

slack.description: How far the outline's chords may stray from the true edges; added to the spacing.

NestingPartEntry.description: How one part was read, and how many of its copies were placed.

reason.description: The part's problem, or tooLargeForAnySheet, noStockLeft, timeBudget or verificationFailed.

NestingLeft.description: Copies of a part that were not placed, and why.

NestingRun.description: How the search ran: whether the same seed gives the same layout again, and whether it was stopped or ran out of time.

NestingReportError.description: The nesting kernel's own answer when it refuses the options or is stopped before any part was nested. No result carries it: the API fails the task with its error instead.

circle.description: The centre's x and y and the radius.

points.description: The vertices as x, y pairs, one after another.

bulges.description: One per vertex: the tangent of a quarter of the arc's angle from that vertex to the next, 0 for a straight line, positive turning counterclockwise.

NestingOutlinePolyline.description: Lines and arcs from vertex to vertex.

majorAxis.description: The vector from the centre to one end of the major axis; its length is the major radius.

ratio.description: The minor radius divided by the major radius.

start.description: Where the arc starts, as the ellipse's parameter t in radians: the point center + cos(t) majorAxis + sin(t) ratio (-majorAxis y, majorAxis x), the minor axis being the major one turned a quarter counterclockwise and scaled by ratio. t is the angle from the major axis only when ratio is 1.

end.description: Where the arc ends, as the same parameter t in radians; the arc runs counterclockwise from start to end, a whole ellipse from 0 to 2 pi.

NestingOutlineEllipse.description: An ellipse or an arc of one.

knots.description: The full knot vector, one more value than the control points and the degree together; the curve starts and ends at its end points.

points.description: The control points as x, y pairs, one after another.

weights.description: One weight per control point when the curve is rational; left out, every weight is 1.

pagination.description: On a continuation sheet, why it continues the sheet before it: a view that did not fit beside the principal views at their scale, or principal views whose annotation letters were too small together.

place.description: The sheet's lower left corner in the DXF and SVG that hold every sheet, in millimetres, y up.

faceless.description: The parts left out of a sheet of every part because they hold no face, such as the curves an AP203 file draws its notes with, when other parts have faces.

index.description: The sheet's index in the whole set, counting from 0; given when the draw named 'onlySheets'.

DrawnSetSheet.description: One sheet as drawn: what the set says of it, where it lies beside the others, its fingerprint and its report.

DrawingResolvedRow.description: One row of an assembly's parts list: its item number from 1, the product's name, how many go directly into the assembly, the product, the index of the sheet that shows it (-1 when none does) and the parts of all its instances.

units.description: The unit the sheet's printed lengths are written in, 'mm' or 'in'. The report's own numbers stay in millimetres.

decimals.description: The places the sheet's printed lengths are written to.

scaleSeries.description: The list the sheet's scale is a step of, one of 'ISO 5455', 'GOST 2.302', 'inch', 'none': 'ISO 5455' for its recommended scales, 'GOST 2.302' for a step of the wider metric series that ISO 5455 does not recommend (1:2.5, 1:4, 1:15, 1:25, 1:40 and the like), 'inch' for the inch series, and 'none' for a scale a plan states that is in no series.

DrawingSheetUsed.description: The sheet as drawn: its size in millimetres, the frame inside its border, the unit and places its lengths are printed in, the scale used and the series it comes from.

DrawingViewUsed.description: One view as drawn: its place on the sheet, its scale and whether it is in line with the base view.

role.description: What the paths are: 'frame' for the frame and, in the margin outside it, an ISO sheet's centring marks and grid reference or an ANSI C, D or E sheet's zones; the model's edges ('sharp', 'outline', 'smooth' and their hidden forms), 'hatch', 'table', 'symbol', 'cut', 'balloon', 'centre', 'dimension', 'note' and 'bend' otherwise.

line.description: 'solid', 'dashed', 'chain', or 'none' for regions to fill rather than lines to draw: a hatch's cut, filled letters, and the dot that ends a balloon's leader on a part.

DrawingGroup.description: One group of paths on the sheet: the view it belongs to (-1 for the sheet's own marks), what it is, its layer, line type, line weight in millimetres and how many paths it holds.

DrawingHatchUsed.description: A hatched cut: the group whose closed paths bound it, the view, the part and the hatch's pattern, angle and spacing.

role.description: What the text is: 'frame' for the letters and numbers of an ISO sheet's grid reference or an ANSI sheet's zones, which stand in the margin outside the frame; 'table', 'symbol', 'cut', 'balloon', 'centre', 'dimension', 'note' or 'bend' for the text of that ink; 'caption' for any other.

DrawingText.description: One text on the sheet: where its baseline starts, its height in millimetres, how far it was narrowed to fit and which end it is anchored by.

DrawingFill.description: A filled triangle, an arrowhead: its three corners as six numbers.

kind.description: 'across' or 'upright' for a size, 'radius' for a radius callout, 'origin' for the X0 Y0 mark of the hole table's origin, 'ordinateX' or 'ordinateY' for an ordinate.

line.description: Two points on the sheet: a size's dimension line; a radius callout's leader from its arrowhead on the arc to where its shoulder starts; an ordinate's extension line from the part to its text.

centre.description: For a radius callout led along its radius, the arc's centre on the sheet; for the origin mark, the middle of the view's box it is led from.

DrawingDimensionUsed.description: One dimension drawn on the sheet: its kind, view, text and line, in millimetres on paper.

given.description: The annotations the sheet draws: all of them, or the named product's.

notes.description: How many stand in the notes area above the title block.

turned.description: How many are drawn reading upside down or from the left.

frontChosen.description: Whether they chose the sheet's front, which they do only when the plan's front is 'annotations'.

elsewhere.description: Annotations no view faces on a sheet whose annotations say addViews false, and general notes of a sheet whose annotations say notes false: another sheet of the set draws them.

DrawingAnnotationsUsed.description: What became of the annotations the STEP file stores.

textHeight.description: The height of the sheet's own text, in millimetres: 2.5 on A4 and A3, 3.5 on A2 and larger, 3 on every ANSI size.

letters.description: The smallest annotation letter on the sheet, in millimetres on paper; 0 for none.

fill.description: The share of the frame the views take, their sizes and captions included.

floors.description: Every floor the sheet breaks, view by view; empty when it reads.

DrawingQuality.description: How the sheet reads, measured on paper: the height of its own text, the smallest annotation letter, how full the frame is, each view's ink, and the floors it breaks with the reason. A setting the plan states is kept even where it breaks a floor, and the floor is named here.

letters.description: The smallest annotation letter on the view, in millimetres on paper; 0 for none.

density.description: The share of the view's box its lines cover, as drawn.

plain.description: The same share at the standard line widths, 0.5 and 0.25 mm.

lines.description: The thick and thin line widths the view is drawn at, in millimetres: 0.35 and 0.18 for a view too dense at the standard ones.

smoothLeftOut.description: Whether the view's smooth edges were left out to thin it.

detailLeftOut.description: How many edges too short to read were left out to thin it.

DrawingViewQuality.description: How one view reads: its smallest annotation letter, how much of it is ink, and what was done to a view too dense to read.

floor.description: 'letters' for annotation letters under the standard height on paper, 2.5 mm (3 mm on ANSI sheets); 'density' for a view whose lines still cover more than a quarter of its box after thinning; 'notes' for general notes that the notes area above the title block holds only with letters under that standard height.

view.description: The view the floor is broken in; -1 for 'notes', which belong to the sheet.

limit.description: The floor it is held to: 2.5 mm for letters (3 mm on ANSI sheets), or 1.8 mm when they are under even that, the standard height for notes, and 0.25 for density.

reason.description: 'constraint' when a setting the plan states keeps the sheet so, 'scale' when no scale of the series reaches the floor on this sheet size.

setting.description: With 'constraint', the setting that keeps it so: 'sheet.scale', 'views[n].scale', 'views' when the view alone on the sheet would reach the floor, or 'annotations.notes' for the notes, which a set hands to a sheet of their own when they have no room; empty with 'scale'.

DrawingFloor.description: A floor of readability the sheet breaks, and why.

methods.description: The method each view was drawn by: 'exact', 'sight' or 'mesh'.

chosenBy.description: For each view, the rule that chose its method, one of 'plan', 'budget', 'within': 'plan' when the plan named the method; with 'auto', 'budget' when the exact method was predicted to take longer than the budget for the sheet, so the view was drawn by sight, and 'within' when it was not, so it was drawn exactly.

DrawingRun.description: How the drawing was made: the hidden-line method, the method each view was drawn by and the rule that chose it, the seconds each view took and, when a view was drawn by sight, what the exact method would have taken.

views.description: For each view, the seconds the exact method was predicted to take on CAD Cloud.

sheet.description: Their sum: what drawing the sheet again with lines.method 'exact' would take on CAD Cloud, about.

DrawingExactEstimate.description: What the exact method was predicted to take on CAD Cloud, given whenever a view was drawn by sight: the drawing kernel predicts the seconds a native build takes, and CAD Cloud's kernel was measured to take 1.2 times as long, so the prediction is given times 1.2. An order of magnitude, not a promise: a single model may take from a tenth to several times it.

DrawingSheetFingerprint.description: The sheet's fingerprint, 64 hexadecimal digits: a SHA-256 over all a sheet is drawn from - the checksum of the STEP file and the unit it is read in, how its parts are read, the sheet's plan as the drawing kernel takes it, the file's annotations it is drawn with, the build of the drawing kernel and the build of the CAD Cloud server that reads the file and writes the sheet's files. Drawing is deterministic: a sheet with the same fingerprint is drawn again the same, written byte for byte as before in its files, with the same report but for 'run', which says how long it took. A deploy of the server gives every sheet a new fingerprint. An app can keep a sheet it drew under its fingerprint, and a sheet whose fingerprint changed is stale.

reused.description: Whether the parts were taken from the model the task named in 'modelFromTask' kept, rather than read from the file.

kept.description: Whether this task kept its model, so that a later draw or inspection of the same file in the same unit can name this task in 'modelFromTask'. Every draw and inspection keeps the model it drew from, one it took from another task included; it is false only when the model could not be kept, and 'notKept' then says why. A kept model is deleted with the task's results when the task expires.

seconds.description: The seconds it took to have the model: to read the file, or to read the kept model.

notReused.description: Given when 'modelFromTask' named a task whose kept model could not be used: why. The file was read instead, and the sheets are the same.

notKept.description: Given when 'kept' is false: why the model could not be kept, such as a model of more than 200 MB or storage that would not take it. The task's results are not affected.

DrawingModelRun.description: Where the model the sheets were drawn from came from, and whether this task kept it.

DrawingSheetFit.description: A standard sheet, whether the plan's views fit it, and the scale an automatic scale would take on it.

DrawingSectionCandidate.description: A section the model could be cut by: what it runs through, its frame, the view that sees it edge-on (-1 when none does), how many parts it cuts and the area cut. Adding its frame to a plan's sections draws it.

parts.description: Every part the sheets draw, in the order of its number, under the product the set draws it as: an unnamed product that holds a single part is merged into the product that places it, so a file of one part below a named product lists the part under that name. A part the set draws under no product, such as loose curves beside solids, is not listed.

DrawingInspectedSet.description: Every sheet of a set written out, each with its fingerprint, the set as a plan with a list of sheets (sent back, it draws the same sheets, with the same fingerprints), and every part with the product it is drawn as.

pagination.description: On a continuation sheet, why it continues the sheet before it: a view that did not fit beside the principal views at their scale, or principal views whose annotation letters were too small together.

DrawingInspectedSheet.description: One sheet of the set an inspection writes out: as the set will draw it, with the fingerprint the sheet will have when the plan of the set is drawn.

DrawingSetPart.description: A part as the set draws it: its number, the product it is drawn as and that product's name as the sheets give it, and which of the product's instances it belongs to, counted from 0 in the order of the model's structure, depth first.

DrawingSavedView.description: A view the STEP file saved (an AP242 model view): its name, which a plan's view gives as 'saved', and how many of the file's annotations it shows.

DrawingModelPart.description: One part of the model: its number, as a plan's parts name it; the name of the product the set draws it as, as the sheets of a set name it ('Part n' for a part the file left unnamed, the uploaded file's name for a file whose root the file left unnamed; an unnamed product holding a single part is merged into the product that places it); the product, by the number a sheet's product takes; and which of the product's instances it belongs to, counted from 0 in the order of the model's structure, depth first, as a plan's annotations count them. A part the set draws under no product, such as loose curves beside solids, has an empty name and neither product nor instance.

DrawingReportError.description: The drawing kernel's own answer when it refuses the plan or cannot draw. No result carries it: the API fails the task with its error instead.

HealthStatus.description: API health check result indicating overall system status

TaskAcceptedResponse.description: HTTP 202 response when a task is accepted for async processing

taskId.description: Unique task identifier - use this to poll for status and retrieve results

statusUrl.description: Relative URL to poll for task status updates

TaskCreatedResult.description: Returned when a CAD task is accepted. Poll the statusUrl to track progress.

ErrorDetail.description: Structured error information with machine-readable code and optional debugging context
